newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty finds comfort in new range.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty finds comfort in new range.

text.p: The zloty slipped into a new trading band between 0.5 and one percent above parity on Tuesday, with resistance guarded by foreigners itching to sell Polish paper at a more favourable exchange rate, dealers said.
They said the zloty's downside would probably be supported by central bank interventions if the zloty approached parity.

"It seems the zloty will not strengthen past one percent as such gains would allow foreigners to exit from Polish paper on better terms and its downside is guarded by expected central bank currency selling interventions," said Malgorzata Sawicka, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 0.75/0.72 percent from the trading band centre, flat from Monday's close at 0.77/0.64 percent. A week earlier the zloty traded around 1.5 percent above parity.
It closed at 3.2885/95 to the dollar, down from 3.2850/90 on Monday and at 1.8842/50 to the mark, up from 1.8835/60.

Foreigners, some of which have been withdrawing from Poland amid calls for a rapid cut of the budget deficit, were not expected to speed up sales when the government officially unveiled its budget outlines for 1998 on Thursday.
"The budget parameters are known and those who wanted to close positions already did so," said one dealer in Warsaw.
Finance Minister Marek Belka proposed a budget deficit of about 1.9 percent of the gross domestic product in 1998 against 2.8 percent gap planned for this year.
The central bank last week said Poland should balance its budget in 1998 in order to avoid a Czech-type crisis.
Poland's 15-percent two year and 12-percent five year fixed bond yields were both expected to grow at Wednesday's joint one billion zloty primary tender on small investor demand.
"Demand for the five year-paper will be very small as foreigners...are more interested in slowly selling Polish paper," said Krzysztof Kozuchowski of ING Bank in Warsaw.

Overnight and tomorrow/next rates eased one point to close at 22.50/23.50 and 22.80/23.20 percent respectively as clearing house outflows improved the market's liquidity in the first days of the July reserve period, dealers said.
The central bank sold one billion zlotys of 91-day NBP-bills at an unchanged average yield of 22.20 percent.
